{{Quote|Don't worry. These hands were programmed by professionals.|[[Unidentified RA-7 protocol droid (Sundered Heart)|An RA-7 protocol droid]], to [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]|<ref name="Memory Loss">{{SWComicCite|7.13|Memory Loss}}</ref>}}
The '''RA-7 protocol droid''', nicknamed the "'''Death Star droid'''," was a low-intelligence model of [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] produced by [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]] specifically for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|This protocol droid is frequently used as an officer's adjutant. RA-7 units keep timetables and maintain schedules, as well as act as translators when foreign emissaries are welcomed aboard ship.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''|<ref name="Handbook" />}}
[[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] in shape with an [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] head, and similar in build to the [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series]] of protocol [[Droid/Legends|droids]], the RA-7 was covered in reflective plating and commonly found in the offices of high-ranking Imperial officials, military officers, courtiers, and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] dignitaries. It was intended to help its owner with scheduling and translating.<ref name="Handbook" /> Unlike 3PO-series with their delicate personalities, RA-7s were programmed to be "stern," but bland.

It had a secret surveillance system installed in its head, hidden beneath layers of benign cognitive circuitry. The espionage unit was hidden behind sensor bafflers that were disguised as soldering welds. It would record everything using extremely sensitive audio pickups and low-light [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and would make periodic dumps of data via encrypted frequencies on standard public comm units to the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="TEGtD" /><ref name="TNEGtD" />

==History==
[[File:Jawas_and_droid_EotE_by_Barrachi.jpg|thumb|left|170px|An RA-7 droid alongside two [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]]]]
{{Quote|And thus I regret to inform your lordship that your gift has been stolen. By a swoop gang, most likely. Or Rebels. Or an alien.|[[Planetary Governor/Legends|Planetary Governor]] [[Furi Nistola]], attempting to explain how he "lost" his Death Star droid|<ref name="TNEGtD" />}}
The RA-7 series was first shown at the [[North Quadrant Intergalactic Automaton Show]] on [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]].<ref name="TNEGtD" /><ref name="Email">{{EmailCite|email=File:EAOC discussion 2023 4.jpg|creator=Jason Fry|date=2023-10-22}}</ref> The model was an attempt by [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]] to duplicate most of the abilities of the 3PO series of protocol droids, and in most aspects it failed. A prototype, [[4A-7/Legends|4A-7]], saw use by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] agent [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].

While not particularly useful, the RA-7 became nearly ubiquitous in the Empire by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] in a plot by the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to spread the droids. The Bureau had ordered thousands of RA-7s from Arakyd and installed special programming in the droids to use them as spies. Almost no one would willingly buy an RA-7 as an assistant&mdash;so the ISB gave them away as gifts. As those targeted by the droids began to uncover hidden recording devices and surveillance equipment in the nigh-useless droids, they began to hide, misplace or lose them to avoid attention and branding as traitors for spurning a gift from the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. This often led them to be found in junk shops, droid auctions, or swap meets.<ref name="TEGtD" /><ref name="TNEGtD" />

A number of RA-7 droids were used aboard [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] to monitor medical equipment, such as [[life support capsule]]s.

[[File:RA7-SWGTCWAoD.jpg|thumb|right|180px|An RA-7 droid serving the Galactic Empire]]
A combination of the destruction of the majority of their droids and the detection of their program caused the Bureau to cancel the RA-7 droid surveillance initiative shortly after [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].

==Ominous nickname==
As the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] came online, the Bureau grew concerned that [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] would attempt to use the superweapon to overthrow the Empire. Unable to trust the Grand Moff or any of his subordinates, the Bureau stationed thousands of RA-7 droids on the Death Star, earning them the nickname "Death Star droids."<ref name="TEGtD" /><ref name="TNEGtD" />

==Behind the scenes==
An RA-7 appears inside the Jawas' sandcrawler after R2-D2 is dropped in after being disabled by the Jawas in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. A second, black-colored RA-7 appears briefly later in the film, walking past [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] outside the Death Star elevator doors.

[[Kenner Products|Kenner]] released a Death Star Droid as part of its second wave of action figures in 1978. The droid was also a [[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|Power of the Force 2]] Freeze Frame Fan Club Exclusive in 1999. Along with the Freeze Frame slide, this black Death Star Droid came packaged with a [[MSE-series|mouse droid]] model.

In [[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]], the adaptation of ''A New Hope'' by [[Marvel Comics]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] tortures [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] with an RA-7 unit rather than an [[IT-O interrogation droid/Legends|IT-O Interrogator]].

In ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'', the "Death Star Droid" can be spawned by typing "npc spawn protocol_imp".

The droid appears, somewhat ironically, as the "guide" droid for the Zann Consortium in the place of where R2, or a black Imperial astromech droid, would in the game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''.
